message.content:
**Time‑zone basics**

| City | Standard offset from UTC | Daylight‑saving offset from UTC |
|------|--------------------------|--------------------------------|
| Los Angeles (PT) | UTC – 8 | UTC – 7 |
| Berlin (CET) | UTC + 1 | UTC + 2 |

**Typical differences**

| When both cities are on standard time | Difference | When both are on daylight time | Difference |
|---------------------------------------|------------|---------------------------------|------------|
| Los Angeles UTC – 8 → Berlin UTC + 1 | **9 hours** (Berlin ahead) | Los Angeles UTC – 7 → Berlin UTC + 2 | **8 hours** (Berlin ahead) |

**Why it can vary**

* **DST start/end dates differ** – Los Angeles begins DST on the second Sunday in March and ends on the first Sunday in November. Berlin starts DST on the last Sunday in March and ends on the last Sunday in October.  
* During those transition weeks the time difference can be **7 or 10 hours**:
  * Early March (before LA switches): 10 h ahead (Berlin + 2 vs LA – 8)
  * Late March/early April (after Berlin switches but before LA): 8 h ahead (Berlin + 2 vs LA – 7)
  * Late October (after Berlin ends but before LA ends): 9 h ahead (Berlin + 1 vs LA – 7)
  * Late October/early November (after LA ends but before Berlin ends): 8 h ahead (Berlin + 1 vs LA – 8)

So, unless you’re looking at a specific date, the most common differences are **9 hours** (standard time) and **8 hours** (daylight time).
